nodes.summary: The likelihood of an alignment of `m` independent columns: the product of the site likelihoods.
nodes.title: Likelihood of an alignment of independent columns

nodes.summary: The leaf data of an alignment column `col : L → S`: the indicator of the observed codon at each leaf.
nodes.title: Leaf data of an alignment column

nodes.summary: Decibans are the natural-log score rescaled by `10 / log 10`.
nodes.title: Deciban score as a rescaled natural-log score

nodes.summary: `10 * log₁₀(L_C / L_N)`, i.e. `(10 / log 10) * score`, since `log₁₀ x = log x / log 10`.
nodes.title: The published PhyloCSF score in decibans

nodes.summary: The score is the log-likelihood ratio of the alignment when all site likelihoods are positive.
nodes.title: The score is the log-likelihood ratio of the alignment

nodes.summary: The threshold test on the score: call the alignment coding (`1`) iff the score exceeds the cutoff `c`.
nodes.title: Score threshold test for calling an alignment coding

nodes.summary: The PhyloCSF score (natural-log scale): the sum over the columns of the log-likelihood ratio of the coding model `(tC, πC)` against the non-coding model `(tN, πN)`. The published PhyloCSF score is reported in decibans; see `score_decibans` for the conversion. Thresholds for this `score` are in natural-log units.
nodes.title: The PhyloCSF score

nodes.summary: Each site likelihood is computed by Felsenstein's pruning algorithm.
nodes.title: Site likelihood by Felsenstein's pruning algorithm

nodes.summary: The likelihood of one alignment column under the model `(t, π)`.
nodes.title: Likelihood of one alignment column

nodes.summary: With positive site likelihoods under both models, a randomized test `φ` whose weighted size under the non-coding weights is at most that of `scoreTest c` has at most its weighted power under the coding weights. This is the dominated Neyman–Pearson inequality for the unnormalized alignment weights `alignLik`; it becomes a statement about statistical size and power only under additional normalization hypotheses (…
nodes.title: PhyloCSF's score threshold test is most powerful for unnormalized weights

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
